concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
question: Which among the following socio religious community was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy?
solution:
The correct answer is __Brahmo Samaj__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which was later renamed Brahmo Samaj.
 
 
• Its chief aim was the worship of the eternal God.
 
 
• It was against priesthood, rituals, and sacrifices.
 
 
 
• It focused on prayers, meditation, and reading the scriptures.
 
 
• It attempted to remove prejudices, negative traditions, and practices against women.
 
 
 
• It was the first intellectual reform movement in modern India.
 
 
• It led to the emergence of rationalism and enlightenment in India which indirectly contributed to the nationalist movement.
 
 
 
• It was the forerunner of all social, religious, and political movements of modern India.
 
 
• It split into two in 1866, namely Brahmo Samaj of India led by Keshub Chandra Sen, and Adi Brahmo Samaj led by Debendranath Tagore.
 
 
 
• Prominent Leaders: Debendranath Tagore, Keshub Chandra Sen, Pt. Sivnath Shastri, and Rabindranath Tagore.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

​__Some Important Socio-religious reform organisations of 19th century are-__

 
 

 
 
Name

 
 
 
Founder and Founding year

 
 
 
Purpose

 
 
 

 
 
Brahmo Samaj

 
 
 
Raja Rammohan Roy, 1828

 
 
 
 
• Hindu socio -reform movement.
 
• Advocated monotheism.
 
• Opposed sati, idolatry and superstition
 
 
 
 

 
 
Young Bengal Movement

 
 
 
Henry Vivian Derozio, 1826-31

 
 
 
 
• Opposed the vices of society.
 
• Believed in truth, freedom and reason.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Rahnumai Mazdayasnan Sabha

 
 
 
 S S Bengali, Naoroji Furdonji, Dadabhai Naoroji

 
 
 
 
• To improve social conditions of Parsis and restore the purity of Zoroastrianism.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Prarthana Samaj

 
 
 
Atmaram Pandurang, Govind Ranade, R G Bhandarkar, 1867

 
 
 
 
• Reform of society, women upliftment, abolition of caste discrimination and religious orthodoxy.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Arya Samaj

 
 
 
Dayanand Saraswati, 1875

 
 
 
 
• Revivalist movement
 
• Gave a call to “go back to vedas”.
 
• Opposed Brahmin supremacy, superstitions and idolatry.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Aligarh Movement

 
 
 
Syed Ahmed Khan

 
 
 
 
• Religious reform in Indian Islam.
 
• Emphasis on critical thinking, reasoning and rational outlook.
 
 
 
 

 
 
The Theosophical Society

 
 
 
H P Blavatsky, H S Olcott, 1875

 
 
 
 
• Religious revival and social reform
 
• Drew Inspiration from Upnishads
 
• Believed in Vedanta
 
 
 
 

 
 
Ramakrishna Mission

 
 
 
Swami Vivekananda, 1897

 
 
 
 
• Hindu religious revival.
 
• Believed in Vedanta philosophy
 
• Opposed superstitions, castism, and oppression.
 
 
 
 

 
 
The Servant of India Society

 
 
 
Gopal Krishna Gokhale, 1905

 
 
 
 
• Famine relief and upliftment of tribals.
 
• Promotion of education, removal of untouchability.
